nodes.description: An angiotensin receptor blocker, alone or with a beta blocker, at maximally tolerated doses is reasonable in Loeys-Dietz syndrome (ACC/AHA class 2a). Beyond lowering haemodynamic stress, the TGFBR1 knock-in mouse provides a pathway rationale: losartan's efficacy tracked suppression of aortic SMAD2 phosphorylation and TGF-beta1 expression, and second heart field-derived smooth muscle cells of the Tgfbr1 mouse up-regulate the angiotensin II type 1 receptor. There are no randomised trials in Loeys-Dietz syndrome. Angiotensin receptor blockers are contraindicated in pregnancy.

nodes.description: The lethal endpoint. In LDS1 and LDS2, type A dissection occurs at younger ages and smaller root diameters than in Marfan syndrome; in a management review pooling LDS types 1-3, dissections have occurred at 3.9-4.0 cm, a figure not specific to TGFBR1 (see the registry result below). In a genotype-split surgical series, type B dissection at the time of initial surgery was much less common in TGFBR1 than TGFBR2 carriers (9.1% vs 54.5%). Dissection is not confined to the aorta: a TGFBR1 carrier presented with, and later had a recurrent, renal artery dissection. Risk is higher in male than female TGFBR1 carriers: in the international registry type A dissection affected 30% of men versus 12% of women, and any aortic event 52% versus 30%, with no such sex effect in TGFBR2 carriers. In the same registry no TGFBR1 carrier of either sex dissected at an aortic root diameter at or below 45 mm.

nodes.description: The primary lesion is a heterozygous germline TGFBR1 variant. In Loeys-Dietz syndrome these are non-truncating - mostly missense or in-frame changes - concentrated in the serine/threonine kinase domain (the founding M318R and D400G alleles lie in it, T200I at the junction with the glycine-serine-rich domain, R487P just C-terminal to it). Tested LDS alleles inactivate canonical TGF-beta signalling and exert a modest dominant-negative effect on co-expressed wild-type receptor. The non-truncating spectrum is what separates LDS1 from multiple self-healing squamous epithelioma, which is caused by truncating TGFBR1 alleles.

nodes.description: Cells heterozygous for an LDS TGFBR1 allele respond less to exogenous TGF-beta in vitro, yet keep normal steady-state SMAD2 phosphorylation, which the knock-in study reads as chronic compensation. This cell-level deficit and its compensations are what set up the tissue-level paradox.

nodes.description: Aortic tissue from TGFBR1/TGFBR2 patients shows nuclear enrichment of phosphorylated SMAD2 with excess collagen and connective tissue growth factor, and pSMAD2 immunostaining is increased in LDS ascending aortas. In Tgfbr1 knock-in mice, aortic-wall SMAD2 phosphorylation and TGF-beta target gene output rise progressively with aneurysm severity, coincide with TGF-beta1 up-regulation, and are suppressed by losartan in proportion to its efficacy; deleting Smad2 in the cardiac neural crest lineage preserves the aortic wall. The excess signalling is therefore placed upstream of the medial lesion. Most of the human tissue evidence pools TGFBR1 and TGFBR2 patients.

nodes.description: Elective (preferably valve-sparing) replacement of the aortic root and ascending aorta before dissection. The 2022 ACC/AHA guideline gives a TGFBR1-specific threshold: an aortic diameter of 4.5 cm or more without high-risk features (class 1), or 4.0 cm or more when high-risk features are present (class 2b) - high-risk features being severe extra-aortic features (craniosynostosis, cleft palate, hypertelorism, bifid uvula, marked tortuosity, widened scars, translucent skin), certain variants, family history of dissection, or growth above 0.3 cm per year.
